name: Metrolink (1985)
description: Midway's Metrolink scheme as the fleet wore it in 1984 and early 1985: an all-white aircraft with no cheatline. On the forward fuselage the Metrolink mark big, just behind the front door: a gray bar over a red one, the red turning down from its forward end in a long diagonal to a point below the windows and a gray stroke inside the angle, so the two read as an M. Behind it 'Midway' in gray bold italic above the windows and 'Metrolink' twice as tall in red heavy italic below them, its first letter tucked under the mark's diagonal. The same mark large on the white fin, heavier and sheared aft, its aft edge on the fin's trailing edge. Gray wings, white nacelles with bare metal lips.

notes: Measured 2026-11-26 for ghost flights on DC-9-31 N931ML (September 1984, right side, side-on) on shapes/DC93.json, with the DC-9-15 (N1064T, April 1984) and MD-81 (N10029, July 1984) measured as types and the 737-200 fitted. The scheme came with the Metrolink business-class branding of 1983 (on N932ML and N10029 by November 1983) and replaced the 1979 striped scheme with the dark blue tail, which the last dated photo found shows in December 1982. Metrolink as a product was dropped in early 1985 but the paint stayed: N1067T still wore it in May 1986. By July 1986 the red scheme was on the fleet's new aircraft and by October 1986 on the DC-9-30s. So in February 1985 the DC-9s and MD-81s wore this. The 737-200s flown then were most likely the ex-Air Florida aircraft of Midway Express at Miami, which wore their own Midway Express scheme (N51AF, October 1984: red and maroon cheatlines, 'Midway Express' titles); no Midway 737 in Metrolink paint was found, so the 737 here is fitted. The aircraft is plain white: no cheatline or belly color on any photo (the lower fuselage reads gray only in shade). The mark is our own simplified drawing (two marks: the body's, and the fin's heavier sheared version). Its red reads from brick to crimson on the slides and the gray from warm gray to charcoal. Titles' heights read within about 0.1 m.

DC91.note: DC-9-15 N1064T (April 1984), seen from ahead so scaled through the perspective by its door and overwing exit: the mark starts right behind the door (about 2.1 m long, 1.95 m tall) and the titles are a little smaller than on N931ML ('Midway' 3.2 m, 'Metrolink' 4.5 m). Within about 0.2 m.
